title: Dixieland band at the club, then Handy's dance-hall jobs and the Alamo
summary: Coaching from Leo Dejan, the Dixieland band's big tips night, then Handy's La Vida band, the Alamo and the foreign dance hall.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Clarence Todd, he did. That's the same song. We can talk to Camilla sometime. Yeah, he was, not so very long ago he was there, you know. Camilla lives uptown. And I also, for Alvin, I got Lois Domain, you know, Lois, I knew you know what it was. I got Lois Domain, what he said then, you know. Well after he sat in the band and taught me, because he used to coach me and tell me a lot of things, he can mention, valuable ideas about the trumpet, little tricks about the trumpet, you know. So after he sat in the band, before he went and played with us that night, he told me, he said, Anderson, I'm telling you what I'm doing, he said, man I'm going to take you and make you the first class trumpet player out of you, you've got to die, you know. He said, I'm going to bring them parts, I'm going to get those parts, make you get those parts down together. So that night when we started playing we had so much music to play, you know, because a young boy used to buy anything. So we had so much music to play that night, when he knocked off that night he said, I changed that. He said, I believe you'd better come over and instruct me. And Camilla Todd, the same way she's the piano player, she took Emily Hines to play, she took him with Aaron and I said, I'm surprised, because we used to play together, we had us in the Dixon Land band, you know. We had Willie Bontem, had Camilla Todd playing piano, had O.L. Foster, my cousin playing drums, I was playing trumpet, a fellow by the name of Gus Smatkart, he played trumpet. We had a nice little outfit, we played at the Columbia Crutch Club, you know. We made some time out there, I remember one night we made nine hours a piece, you know. Our side was fifteen hours, we left there with nine hours a piece, including our tips, you know. And one of those doctors tipped us so much he was kind of tipsy that night, you know, he just got a little bit too much in it. He wanted to play drums, nothing even wanted to play those drums, see. And the people in the place didn't want to play drums, you know. And every time he danced around he'd hand the drum about a ten dollar bill, see. He said, I guess that would make me play drums. So the drummer would let him play drums, see. And through that way we all got a plenty of tips. So what we knew him after that, we didn't like Doc, because Doc was a fine man, I said. So the next time Doc came in there, all of us hollering, hey Doc, how are you? He said, I think I said, all of you can go to hell. He said, I'm not drinking tonight. So don't be out of hand. So, after I left that bunch there, Handy took me off the Pelican. I said, I was playing on the Pelican, I was leading the band there, the Pelican band there, after the program left. Handy took me off the Pelican. He played the La Vida dance hall, the taxi dance. Alfred was playing drums there. He had Alfred playing drums, Handy the sax, Benny Turner playing piano, had I forget, one of the Hall brothers, you know, Clarence Hall, Edmund Hall, or the other brother, Robert Hall playing tenor. And we had, let's see, I think it was Manuel Sills playing guitar, yeah. He was playing banjo there, Manuel Sills, yeah. And I was playing trumpet. Well, I stayed there with them all about a year or so. So after, I tell you what, we went there one night to go to work, you know, and this guy, I forget his name, went to go to work and the place was locked on Monday night, which was pig night, see. So we went to the labor board to find us, and the man told us, I tell you one thing, these fellas fly by the night fellas, you all got to be careful playing for them. So some of them just in his business and said, soon as they make a good night, they're gone, you know. We never did get paid for that last week, I tell you. So what happened, we went to, the fella hired me at the Alamo dance hall. Well, Handy still kept his band. Handy had his Louisiana shaker, see. He had Alvin Alcorn with me, he went one way and I went on the Alamo, on the Canal Street, on Canal and Begun upstairs there, over at McCroys store there, it was Alamo there. Well I played there for quite a time, I think I must have played there about four years, around four years or something like that. And the man was running that place, took the Levita, Mr. Boyd took the Levita, see. Well I still work on the Levita for him, I went to the Levita for him after that. Played at the Levita. And from the Levita Gene Hall came in town and they hired me to play at the foreign dance hall, which is next door. Well at that time it was the Budweiser, the Budweiser people I had interest in, they had that great big eagle there, you know, on the outside. Well I was playing in that and old man they used to have some crowds and people in there. They had a bike in the back and a patio there. Place packed and jammed every night, you know, people made something out of that. And little young Danny got in a fight there with some soldier or something and hit the soldier.
